Nikolai Yezhov: NKVD director under Joseph Stalin (1895–1940)
Born in Iran and raised in Germany, this politician co-led the Greens alongside Ricarda Lang and has served as Vice President of the Bundestag since 2025 — who is he?

Born to a Tutsi family that fled to Uganda when he was two, this politician commanded a rebel force that ended the 1994 genocide in his home country and has served as its president since 2000 — who is he?
Paul Kagame: President of Rwanda since 2000. The RPF was one of the main belligerents of the Rwandan Civil War and was the armed force which ended the 1994 Rwandan genocide.
The first Kerala Chief Minister to win re-election after completing a full term, this CPI(M) leader represented the Dharmadom constituency — who is he?
Which Chinese diplomat rocketed to foreign minister in December 2022, then vanished from public view six months later and was quietly removed by July 2023?
Co-founded by Nigel Farage in 2018 as the Brexit Party before its later renaming, this British party now holds seven seats in the Commons — name it?
Reform UK: Political party in the United Kingdom.
A media consultant for three Republican presidents, this longtime Fox News chairman had hemophilia, a condition that complicated the injury that eventually caused his 2017 death — who was he?
Roger Ailes: American TV executive and consultant (1940–2017)
A Kurdish commander who founded the Ayyubid dynasty and became the first sultan of both Egypt and Syria, he led the Muslim effort during the Third Crusade — who is he?
Saladin: Founder of the Ayyubid dynasty (c. 1137–1193)

Considered history's largest colonial campaign, this 1935–36 conflict saw two hundred thousand invading troops attack without a declaration, retaking a town that symbolized their army's earlier defeat there four decades before. Which conflict?
Second Italo-Ethiopian War: 1935–1936 war between Italy and Ethiopia.
Grandson of a prime minister and the longest-serving PM in his nation's history, this Japanese politician led the Liberal Democratic Party across two stints in office — who was he?
Shinzo Abe: Prime Minister of Japan (2006–2007; 2012–2020)
The only communist state ever to exist in the Arab world, this nation in southern Arabia had its capital at Aden before unifying with its northern neighbor in 1990 — what was it?
South Yemen: 1967–1990 state in Western Asia.
Around 986 he revolted against his father Harald Bluetooth to seize Denmark's throne, and in December 1013 briefly became King of England too — which Viking ruler was it?
Swein Forkbeard: King of Denmark and England (died 1014)
Often appearing as a crow and said to wash the bloodstained clothes of those fated to die in battle, which Irish goddess of war and fate is known as the 'phantom queen'?
The Morrígan: Figure from Irish mythology.
The only person to lead Labour to three consecutive general election victories, this MP for Sedgefield served as UK prime minister from 1997 to 2007 — who is he?
Tony Blair: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 1997 to 2007.
This Portuguese nobleman opened the first direct sea route from Europe to India, rounding the Cape of Good Hope and crossing the Indian Ocean from Malindi in Kenya to Kozhikode. Who is he?
This Elizabethan explorer and statesman helped defend England against the Spanish Armada while also playing a leading role in colonizing North America — who was he?
Walter Raleigh: English statesman and explorer (1552–1618)

He started as a wildly successful Scottish privateer, commissioned by the governor of New York to hunt pirates and French ships in the Indian Ocean from his ship Adventure Galley — which sea captain, hanged in 1701, is it?
William Kidd: Scottish privateer (1654–1701). William Kidd (c. 1645 – 23 May 1701), also known as Captain William Kidd or simply Captain Kidd, was a Scottish privateer.
After defeating the last Zagwe king around 1270, this ruler founded Ethiopia's Solomonic dynasty, which would endure until 1974 — who is he?
Yekuno Amlak: Emperor of Ethiopia from 1270 to 1285.
This French lawyer-turned-politician served as prime minister under Emmanuel Macron from 2017 to 2020, then returned to serve as mayor of Le Havre — who is he?
Édouard Philippe: Prime Minister of France from 2017 to 2020. A lawyer by occupation, Philippe is a former member of the Union for a Popular Movement (UMP), which later became The Republicans (LR).
Which of these people was born first?
Thomas Carlyle (born 1795) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Saint Valentine (born 175) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these was founded earliest?
Bash (Unix shell) (founded 1989) is the earliest of the four.
C (programming language) (founded 1972) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these is an astronomer?
Stephen Gray (scientist) is an astronomer. Stephen Gray (December 1666 – February 1736) was an English dyer and astronomer who was the first to systematically experiment with electrical conduction.
Which of these four is a mathematician?
Nicholas Georgescu-Roegen is a mathematician. Nicholas Georgescu-Roegen (born Nicolae Georgescu, 4 February 1906 – 30 October 1994) was a Romanian mathematician, statistician and economist.
What is the atomic number of Dubnium?
Dubnium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Db and atomic number 105.
What is the atomic number of Iridium?
Iridium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ir and atomic number 77.
In what year was B. R. Ambedkar born?
B. R. Ambedkar: Ambedkar served as Law and Justice minister in the first cabinet of Jawaharlal Nehru.
In what year was Hedy Lamarr born?
Hedy Lamarr (born Hedwig Eva Maria Kiesler; November 9, 1914 – January 19, 2000) was an Austrian and American actress and inventor.
In what year was Erwin Schrödinger born?
Erwin Schrödinger: Schrödinger shared the 1933 Nobel Prize in Physics with Paul Dirac "for the discovery of new productive forms of atomic theory".
In what year did William Howard Taft die?
William Howard Taft: Taft attended Yale and joined Skull and Bones, of which his father was a founding member.
In what year did Karl Marx die?
Karl Marx: Born in Trier in the Kingdom of Prussia, Marx earned a doctoral degree in philosophy from the University of Jena in 1841.
In what year was Fluorine discovered?
Fluorine is a chemical element; it has symbol F and atomic number 9.
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-15: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. The MiG-15 was one of the first successful jet fighters to incorporate swept wings to perform near Mach 1.
Which country is Panavia Tornado from?
Panavia Tornado: Italy. It first flew on 14 August 1974 and was introduced into service in 1979–1980.
Who is credited with discovering Phoenix?
Phoenix (constellation): Petrus Plancius. Named after the mythical phoenix, it was first depicted on a celestial atlas by Johann Bayer in his 1603 Uranometria.
Who is credited with discovering Glycerol?
Glycerol: Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Glycerol is a sugar alcohol with chemical formula C3H5(OH)3.
Who is credited with discovering Theory of relativity?
Theory of relativity: Albert Einstein. Special relativity applies to all physical phenomena in the absence of gravity.
Who is credited with discovering Sombrero Galaxy?
Sombrero Galaxy: Pierre Méchain. It is a member of the Virgo II Groups, a series of galaxies and galaxy clusters strung out from the southern edge of the Virgo Supercluster.
In chemistry, this class is defined by an −OH group that lends water-loving properties to otherwise water-shy hydrocarbons, spanning everything from ethanol to sugar versions — what is it?
Alcohol (chemistry) (from Arabic al-kul 'the kohl') is a type of organic compound that carries at least one hydroxyl (OH) functional group bound to a saturated carbon atom.
Closely related to Hepatica and Pulsatilla, which flowering plant genus in the buttercup family is nicknamed the windflower?
Anemone is a genus of flowering plants in the buttercup family Ranunculaceae.

In 2003, this American mountaineer amputated his own trapped forearm with a dull pocket knife after five days pinned by a boulder in a Utah canyon, then rappelled and hiked miles to safety — who is he?

Aron Ralston (born October 27, 1975) is an American mountaineer, mechanical engineer, and motivational speaker, known for surviving a canyoneering accident in 2003 by cutting off part of his own right arm.
This facial hair grows on the jaw, chin, and cheeks, most commonly in adult men, though some women develop it too in a condition called hirsutism — name it?
Beard is the hair that grows on the jaw, chin, upper lip, lower lip, cheeks, and neck of humans and some non-human animals.
This insect order contains both cockroaches and termites — the latter now classified as a specialized, social lineage within the former group — what order is it?
Blattodea is an order of insects that contains cockroaches and termites.
Affecting roughly 22% of people worldwide and often striking during sleep, this parafunctional habit grinds teeth and clenches jaws until enamel wears away — what's it called?
Bruxism is excessive teeth grinding or jaw clenching.

This American astronomer and planetary scientist was initially an assistant professor at Harvard before moving to Cornell as the David Duncan Professor of Astronomy. He played an active role in the Voyager programs. Who is he?
Carl Sagan (November 9, 1934 - December 20, 1996) was an American astronomer, planetary scientist and science communicator.

Once prized as refrigerants and aerosol propellants — Freon being the famous example — these halogenated compounds were phased out under the Montreal Protocol for gnawing holes in the ozone layer — what are they?
Chlorofluorocarbon (CFCs) and hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFCs) are fully or partly halogenated hydrocarbons that contain carbon (C), hydrogen (H), chlorine (Cl), and fluorine (F).
In mathematics, this term describes a selection of items from a set in which the order of choosing doesn't matter — unlike its counterpart, the permutation. Name the concept?
Combination is a selection of items from a set that has distinct members, such that the order of selection does not matter (unlike permutations).

This practice and field of study focuses on techniques for secure communication in the presence of adversaries, sitting at the intersection of mathematics, computer science, and electrical engineering — what's the field called?
Cryptography is the practice and study of techniques for secure communication in the presence of adversarial behavior.
A colorless liquid that's a workhorse solvent for chemical reactions, this compound is officially odorless — yet degraded samples reek of fish thanks to a dimethylamine impurity; what is it?
Dimethylformamide is an organic compound with the chemical formula HCON(CH3)2.

Specializing in legislative process and authoritarian rule, this Russian scholar became a fellow at a Berlin academy and hosts her own political radio talk show, reaching a million YouTube subscribers by 2022 — who is she?
Ekaterina Schulmann (ne Zaslavskaya; born 19 August 1978) is a Russian political scientist specializing in legislative processes and authoritarian governance.

This branch of anthropology systematically studies individual cultures from the point of view of the people within them, relying heavily on researchers directly participating in the settings they study — what is this method called?
Ethnography is a branch of anthropology and the systematic study of individual cultures. It explores cultural phenomena from the point of view of the subject of the study.
This everyday bodily process — expelling gas from the intestines through the anus — has its own dedicated field of scientific study named after it: what's the term for the process itself?
Flatulence is the expulsion of gas from the intestines via the anus, commonly referred to as farting.
Its name comes from Greek words meaning "study of the earth," and this science examines the rocks and processes that shape not just our planet but other astronomical bodies too — what field is it?
Geology is a branch of natural science concerned with the Earth and other astronomical bodies, the rocks of which they are composed, and the processes by which they change over time.
This Italian-American motorsport boss ran a Formula One team for seven years before becoming CEO and owner of a MotoGP outfit — who is he?
Guenther Steiner (born 7 April 1965) is an Italian and American motorsport engineer and former team manager.
This seasonal state of low body temperature, slow breathing, and reduced metabolism helps some animals pass through winter months — what is it?
Hibernation is a state of minimal activity and metabolic reduction entered by some animal species.

Worldwide, too little dietary iodine is the leading cause of this endocrine condition, in which a sluggish thyroid leaves people cold-intolerant, exhausted, constipated, and prone to weight gain — what is it?
Hypothyroidism is an endocrine disease in which the thyroid gland does not produce enough thyroid hormones.
The biggest cat in the Americas, it kills with a bite so powerful it can crack a turtle's shell — or punch straight through a mammal's skull between the ears. Which spotted predator is it?
Jaguar (Panthera onca) is a large cat species and the only living member of the genus Panthera that is native to the Americas.
This occupation and set of methods involves producing and distributing reports on events and people that make up the 'news of the day,' with a commitment to accuracy — what is it?
Journalism is the production and distribution of reports on events, facts, ideas, and people that constitute the "news of the day" and inform society with a commitment to accuracy and verification.
What reddish-brown, alcohol-based tincture of opium, roughly 10% opium by weight, was historically sold without a prescription as a pain reliever and cough suppressant until the early 20th century?
Laudanum is a tincture of opium containing approximately 10% powdered opium by weight (the equivalent of 1% morphine).
Used since pre-Columbian times as a pack animal that can haul about a quarter of its body weight for miles, which domesticated South American camelid has wool low in lanolin?
Llama (Spanish) (Lama glama) is a domesticated South American camelid, widely used as a meat and pack animal by Andean cultures since the pre-Columbian era.
Though it's the strongest bone in the face, this lower jawbone tends to deform with age and is prone to fractures — what is it called?

Mandible (from the Latin mandibula, 'for chewing'), lower jaw, or jawbone is a bone that makes up the lower - and typically more mobile - component of the mouth (the upper jaw being known as the maxilla).

This cluster of at least three conditions -- including high blood sugar, high triglycerides, and low 'good' cholesterol -- raises heart disease and diabetes risk in roughly a quarter of American adults. What is it called?

Metabolic syndrome is a clustering of at least three of the following five medical conditions: abdominal obesity, high blood pressure, high blood sugar, high serum triglycerides, and low serum high-density lipoprotein (HDL).
This genus of edible sac fungi has a honeycomb-like cap of ridges and pits, is prized in French and Catalan cooking, and turns toxic if eaten raw or undercooked. What fungus is this?
Morchella is a genus of edible sac fungi closely related to anatomically simpler cup fungi in the order Pezizales (division Ascomycota).

First arising in wormlike creatures some 550 million years ago, this body-wide network coordinates actions and relays sensory signals through a central half and a peripheral half — what system is being described?
Nervous system is the highly complex part of an animal that coordinates its actions and sensory information by transmitting signals to and from different parts of its body.

This branch of medicine focuses on the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of cancer, a disease first documented in Egypt as early as 3000 BCE in the Edwin Smith papyrus — what is this medical specialty called?
Oncology is a branch of medicine that deals with the study, treatment, diagnosis, and prevention of cancer.
Designed by Niklaus Wirth to encourage structured programming and named after a French mathematician-philosopher, this language was developed in the pattern of ALGOL 60 — name it?

Pascal (programming language) is an imperative and procedural programming language, designed by Niklaus Wirth as a small, efficient language intended to encourage good programming practices using structured programming and data structuring.

Associated with the early 20th century, this philosophical movement tries to objectively describe subjective conscious experience exactly as it appears, without assuming anything about the outside world — which movement?
Phenomenology (philosophy) is a philosophical study and movement largely associated with the early 20th century that seeks to objectively investigate the nature of subjective, conscious experience.

It plays out everywhere from the clans of traditional societies up through modern governments, and its practitioners negotiate, make laws, and sometimes wage war; what is this activity of settling a society's affairs?
Politics is the activity of settling affairs in an organized society. Politics is usually concerned with resolving issues within a society via a government.
This Gram-negative, rod-shaped bacterium selectively blocks antibiotics from crossing its outer membrane, making it a notorious cause of hospital-acquired pneumonia — what is it?
Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a common encapsulated, Gram-negative, aerobic-facultatively anaerobic, rod-shaped bacterium that can cause disease in plants and animals, including humans.
Named from the Latin word for 'net', this light-sensitive layer lining the back of the eye functions much like the film or sensor inside a camera. Name this part of the eye?
One of the world's oldest crops, this thistle-like annual plant with globular orange or red flower heads is grown commercially today for oil pressed from its seeds — what is it?
Safflower (Carthamus tinctorius), also false saffron, is a highly branched, herbaceous, thistle-like annual plant in the family Asteraceae.
Applied practically by Archimedes for the quadrature of a parabola, what do we call the addition of infinitely many terms, one after another, central to calculus?
Series (mathematics) is, roughly speaking, an addition of infinitely many terms, one after the other.
Which genus of about 28 grass species includes one member grown worldwide both as a cereal grain for human consumption and as fodder for livestock?
Sorghum (genus) is a genus of about 28 species of flowering plants in the grass family (Poaceae).
This towering perennial grass, native to New Guinea, stores so much natural sweetness in its jointed stalks that it's the world's primary source for a common sweetener — what plant is it?
Sugarcane is a species of tall, perennial grass (in the genus Saccharum, tribe Andropogoneae) that is used for sugar production.

Named for the order of fish that includes pufferfish, this potent neurotoxin also turns up in blue-ringed octopuses and rough-skinned newts, and is actually produced by symbiotic bacteria rather than the animals themselves — what's the toxin?

Tetrodotoxin (TTX) is a potent neurotoxin. Its name derives from Tetraodontiformes, an order that includes pufferfish, porcupinefish, ocean sunfish, and triggerfish; several of these species carry the toxin.

This American businessman co-founded and served as CEO of a ride-hailing company from 2010 to 2017, resigning amid harassment allegations, and now runs a ghost-kitchen operator called CloudKitchens — who is he?
Travis Kalanick (born August 6, 1976) is an American businessman best known as the co-founder and former chief executive officer (CEO) of Uber.
Native only to the wetlands of the Carolinas, which carnivorous plant snaps shut a 'jaw' formed from the tips of its leaves when an insect trips it?
Venus flytrap (Dionaea muscipula) is a carnivorous plant native to the temperate and subtropical wetlands of North Carolina and South Carolina, on the East Coast of the United States.
This noble gas, found in trace amounts in Earth's atmosphere, powers arc lamps, serves as a rare anesthetic, and was the first of its family coaxed into a genuine chemical compound — which element?
Xenon is a chemical element; it has symbol Xe and atomic number 54.
Unearthed in Montana by Jack Horner's team in 1987, this 20-foot horned dinosaur sported a bony neck-frill and lived roughly 75 million years ago — which species?
Achelousaurus: Genus of ceratopsid dinosaur from North America.
Often called the father of theoretical computer science, this Englishman gave us a famous 'machine' that formalized the very idea of computation — who was he?

Nicknamed 'lazy eye,' this childhood vision disorder occurs when the brain favors one eye over the other, and correcting the underlying cause doesn't restore sight right away — what is this condition?
Amblyopia: Failure of the brain to process input from one eye.
This American anthropologist studied women's weaving and blacksmithing work in Indonesia and later designed microcredit programs to fight rural poverty — who was she?
Native to the Philippines and spread by Austronesian voyagers as early as 1500 BCE, this palm's fruit is chewed with slaked lime and betel leaves for its stimulant effects — which species?
Areca catechu: Species of palm. It was carried widely through the tropics by the Austronesian migrations and trade since at least 1500 BCE due to its use in betel nut chewing.
Developed to herd livestock across rough terrain by nipping at their heels, this short-coated working breed's coat reads as either 'red' or 'blue' — which breed?

Australian Cattle Dog: Breed of herding dog. The Australian Cattle Dog, or simply Cattle Dog, is a breed of herding dog developed in Australia for droving cattle over long distances across rough terrain.

This relationship, expressed as A = εcl, links how much light a solution absorbs directly to its concentration — what is this principle called, named after two scientists whose work dates back to the mid-18th century?
Beer–Lambert law: Scientific law describing absorption of light.
Not a species of its own, it's really a melanistic leopard or jaguar whose rosettes are still hidden under the dark coat — what do we call this big-cat colour variant?
Black panther: Variant of leopard and jaguar. Black panthers of both species have excess black pigments, but their typical rosettes are also present.
This subfamily of horned, cloven-hooved ungulates includes cattle, bison, and both African and water buffalo, with the gaur as its largest living member — which group?
In 1930, which Indian physicist won the Nobel Prize for discovering that light changes wavelength when passing through a transparent material, becoming the first Asian to win a Physics Nobel?

Defined by a –COOH functional group attached to an R-group, and only partially dissociating in water, this general class of organic compounds includes fatty compounds and the building blocks of proteins — what is this functional class called?
Carboxylic acid: Organic compound containing a –C(=O)OH group.
Often called the Judas tree, this small deciduous redbud native to Southern Europe and Western Asia bursts into deep pink blossoms each spring — what species is it?

Caused by a bacterium spread through contaminated water and undercooked shellfish, this intestinal infection produces severe watery diarrhea that can trigger dehydration within hours — which disease is it?
Cholera: Bacterial infection of the small intestine.
Commonly called the tailbone, this bone is the vestigial remnant of a tail in humans and other tailless primates, sitting just below the sacrum — which bone?
Coccyx: Bone of the pelvis. In tailless primates (e.g. humans and other great apes) since Nacholapithecus (a Miocene hominoid), the coccyx is the remnant of a vestigial tail.
One of the few metals found in nature in directly usable metallic form, this soft, pinkish-orange element with symbol Cu prizes its high thermal and electrical conductivity — what is it?
Copper: Chemical element with atomic number 29 (Cu)
Caused by prolonged exposure to excess cortisol, this condition produces abdominal weight gain with thin limbs, a rounded red face, and reddish stretch marks — which condition is it?
Cushing's syndrome: Symptoms from excessive exposure to glucocorticoids such as cortisol.

Known mainly through DNA evidence rather than plentiful fossils, this extinct archaic human group ranged across Asia until about 32,000 years ago, and DNA analysis confirmed the Harbin skull belonged to it — what group is it?
Denisovan: Archaic human species from Asia.
In 1949, this NASA mathematician became the first African-American woman to supervise a team at Langley, later teaching herself and her staff the Fortran language — who is she?
Dorothy Vaughan: American human computer and computer programmer (1910–2008)
Known as aubergine or brinjal elsewhere, this purple, spongy fruit in the nightshade family is technically a berry despite usually being cooked as a vegetable — what is it?
A German Jew who fled the Nazi regime, this social psychologist and democratic socialist helped found a psychoanalytic institute in New York and was linked to the Frankfurt School — who is he?
Once widespread during the Pleistocene and later reintroduced by humans to its ancient range, which hoofed mammal species is native to Turkey and possibly Italy, the Balkans, and Rhodes?
European fallow deer: Species of hooved mammal. The European fallow deer (Dama dama), also known as the common fallow deer or simply fallow deer, is a species of deer native to Eurasia.
This genus of about 850 tropical tree, shrub, and vine species is best known for two cultivated fruit-bearing members and serves as a vital food source for wildlife across the tropics — which genus?
Ficus: Genus of flowering plants in the mulberry family Moraceae.
Native from the British Isles east to the Caucasus, this tree in the olive family is prized for wood that's flexible, strong, and lightweight — what is its scientific name?
Fraxinus excelsior: Species of deciduous tree.
Dubbed "the Godfather of AI" for his pioneering work on neural networks, this Nobel laureate quit Google in 2023 to warn about AI's risks. Who is he?
Caused by the bacterium Neisseria gonorrhoeae and colloquially called 'the clap,' this sexually transmitted infection can pass from mother to child during birth — what is it?
Gonorrhea: Sexually transmitted infection. Gonorrhea or gonorrhoea, colloquially known as the clap, is a sexually transmitted infection (STI) caused by the bacterium Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
This North Atlantic member of the true cod family is prized smoked as Finnan haddie or the Arbroath smokie — what fish is it?
Haddock: Species of fish. The haddock (Melanogrammus aeglefinus) is a saltwater ray-finned fish from the family Gadidae, the true cods.
This inflammation of the liver can cause jaundice and, if it becomes chronic, progress to cirrhosis — most commonly caused by five different viruses labeled A through E. What condition is it?
Hepatitis: Inflammation of the liver. Hepatitis is acute if it resolves within six months, and chronic if it lasts longer than six months.
The most widespread of all primates, this bipedal, nearly hairless species owes its advanced technology, culture, and language to a large, complex brain — what is it?
Human: Species of hominid in the genus Homo.

Extracted from a Central African plant sacred to Gabon's Bwiti tradition, this hallucinogenic alkaloid was once marketed in Europe as a stimulant before being studied for other therapeutic uses — what is it?
Ibogaine: Psychoactive substance found in plants in the family Apocynaceae.

A theoretical physicist who studied under Max Born earned a chemistry degree from Harvard before pivoting to nuclear physics — and later oversaw the first atomic weapons during WWII. Who is this pivotal figure in physics history?
J. Robert Oppenheimer: American theoretical physicist (1904–1967)
In a landmark 1913 Columbia University address, this American psychologist championed behaviorism and later became known for the unsettling 'Little Albert' experiment — who is he?
Nicknamed 'The Professor' on The Chase, this record-breaking contestant won 74 consecutive games on a legendary quiz show in 2004 before eventually becoming its host — who is he?
Ken Jennings: American game show host (born 1974)
Native to North America and infamous for occasionally eating their mates after reproduction, the females of this venomous spider species sport striking black-and-red coloring — what species is it?
Latrodectus mactans: Species of spider. Latrodectus mactans, known as southern black widow or simply black widow, and the shoe-button spider, is a venomous species of spider in the genus Latrodectus.
This big cat of the genus Panthera now ranges only in Sub-Saharan Africa and India, and is unusual among wild cats for living in social groups — what is it?
Lion: Large cat native to Africa and India.
Located near the backbone on either side of the heart, this organ extracts oxygen from the air and releases carbon dioxide, driven mainly by the diaphragm — which organ is it?
Lung: Primary organ of the respiratory system.
This sugar alcohol pulls double duty as a low-calorie sweetener and a drug given by injection to lower pressure in the eyes or inside the skull — an osmotic diuretic. What is it?
Native to Indomalaya and Australasia, this deciduous member of the mahogany family goes by names like chinaberry tree and Persian lilac — what is it?
Succeeding the Castro brothers, this engineer became Cuba's first head of state in nearly six decades who wasn't a member of that family — who is he?
Miguel Díaz-Canel: Leader of Cuba since 2021.
Sold under the brand name Singulair, this asthma medication blocks leukotriene D4 in the lungs but received a UK black box warning in 2019 over neuropsychiatric side effects — what is it?
Montelukast: Medication used in asthma or COPD.
This genus of venomous elapid snakes across Africa and Asia is home to the 'true cobras' — after a 2009 taxonomic revision folded in two other genera, it now contains 38 species — which genus?
Naja: Genus of snakes. Until recently, the genus Naja had 20 to 22 species, but it has undergone several taxonomic revisions in recent years, so sources vary greatly.
Colourless and odourless, this element pairs with itself to form a diatomic gas that makes up about 78% of the air you're breathing — what is it?
Nitrogen: Chemical element with atomic number 7 (N)
Born in Nishapur during the Seljuk era, this Persian polymath solved general cubic equations using intersecting conic sections centuries before Descartes — who was he?
Omar Khayyam: Persian polymath and poet (1048–1131)
A perennial herb from the mountains of East Asia, its root is the original source of a famous herbal supplement — though studies find little evidence it actually works. Which plant?
Panax ginseng: Species of flowering plant.
Commonly called geraniums or storksbills, this genus of roughly 280 evergreen species was split from a related genus by a botanist in 1789 — which genus, native largely to southern Africa?
Pelargonium: Genus of plants. It includes about 280 species of perennials, succulents, and shrubs.

Nicknamed 'terror birds,' this family of large, mostly flightless carnivores roamed the Americas from the Cenozoic era, with one genus, Titanis, reaching as far as the southern United States — which family?
Phorusrhacidae: Extinct family of flightless birds. The exact number of genera is uncertain, as some taxa such as Brontornis may be different forms of bird instead.

Proposed in 1904 and finally proven a century later using Richard Hamilton's Ricci flow techniques, this problem asks whether any loop-shrinkable finite 3D space must be a hypersphere — which famous problem?
Poincaré conjecture: Theorem in geometric topology.
Nearly odorless with a faintly sweet taste, this diol is approved as a food additive under E-number E1520 and serves as a solvent vehicle in many medications — which compound?
Propylene glycol: Chemical compound. Propylene glycol (IUPAC name: propane-1,2-diol) is a viscous, colorless liquid.
Also known as the holly oak, this large evergreen tree native to the Mediterranean produces acorns that mature within a single summer — which species is it?
Quercus ilex: Oak tree species native to the Mediterranean.

Found in fish, dairy, and meat, this fat-soluble vitamin A derivative is prescribed for xerophthalmia and used topically in anti-wrinkle skincare — but too much during pregnancy can harm the fetus. What is it?
Once used by German butchers to herd cattle and pull meat carts to market, this mastiff-type breed now works as a search-and-rescue and police dog — which breed?
Rottweiler: Large German dog breed. The Rottweiler (UK also, German: [ˈʁɔtvaɪ̯lɐ]) is a breed of domestic mastiff type dog, regarded as medium-to-large or large.

Discovered in 1879 via spectral analysis of Scandinavian minerals, this silvery-white rare-earth element with atomic number 21 wasn't isolated in metallic form until 1937, and today it's prized for strengthening aluminum alloys — which element?
Scandium: Chemical element with atomic number 21 (Sc)
This body of religious law, drawn from the Qur'an and hadith, refers to immutable divine law — distinct from fiqh, its human interpretation by scholars. What is it?
Sharia: Islamic law. Approaches to Sharia in the 21st century vary widely, and the role and mutability of Sharia in a changing world has become an increasingly debated topic in Islam.

Historically mined in vast deposits and nicknamed 'Chile saltpeter,' this white, water-soluble alkali metal compound is used in fertilizers, fireworks, meat preservation, and solid rocket fuel. What is it?
Sodium nitrate: Chemical compound. The mineral form is also known as nitratine, nitratite or soda niter.
Derived from the Greek word for 'narrow,' this medical term describes the abnormal tightening of a blood vessel or other tubular structure — what is it?
Stenosis: Medical condition. Stenosis (from Ancient Greek στενός (stenós) 'narrow') is the abnormal narrowing of a blood vessel or other tubular organ or structure such as foramina and canals.
